builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SACQ: Structure-Aware Codebook Quantization for Ultra-Low-Bit Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: SACQ replaces standard LLM-inherited post-training weight quantization (e.g., uniform GPTQ-style recipes) for Vision-Language-Action models with structure-aware vector-codebook fitting, action-error-driven mixed-bit allocation, and a two-stage codeword and scale refinement calibrated against decoded actions. The cost is a multi-stage quantization pipeline requiring calibration data, per-layer sensitivity measurement through the action head, and reimplementation of codebook fitting rather than an off-the-shelf PTQ call; activation quantization and low-precision attention add further engineering. It can fail when the target model or task distribution differs from GR00T N1.7 and LIBERO/SimplER, since codebooks and bit allocations are fitted to specific input statistics and downstream action sensitivity, and results do not generalize to non-VLA LLM workloads.
rationale: The gains are demonstrated only on robotic VLA models with task-specific calibration, so the method is relevant only if the reader deploys VLAs; for general LLM quantization on a 24 GB GPU, mature PTQ tools remain the practical choice.
technique: Structure-aware ultra-low-bit vector quantization for VLA models
